name: Corporate Acquisition Likelihood Model
description: This dataset provides predictive rankings of publicly traded companies most likely to be acquired within the next year. It leverages both advanced natural language processing of global news articles and analysis of structured financial and corporate data, including M&A activity, proxy fights, credit risk, and valuation metrics. By combining text-based signals with fundamental indicators, the model offers percentile scores across global, regional, sector, and industry levels, as well as flags for recent corporate actions. Investors and analysts can use these insights to identify potential takeover targets, anticipate price movements driven by acquisition speculation, and inform event-driven trading strategies.

name: AI Enhanced Equity Factor Transfer
description: This dataset leverages advanced AI techniques to extract and transfer high-level equity factor features from a sophisticated quantitative research framework to other datasets. It includes a rich set of features such as price momentum, money flow strength, volume anomalies, liquidity alignment, and technical indicators like Bollinger Bands and Williams %R. Each feature is semantically defined and generated through AI-driven processes, ensuring clarity and consistency. By capturing nuanced interactions between price, volume, and liquidity, the dataset provides actionable signals for predicting price movements and constructing robust quantitative models. Its transfer learning approach enables the application of proven factor knowledge across diverse datasets, enhancing the predictive power and adaptability of investment strategies.

name: AI News Sentiment Scores
description: This dataset provides daily sentiment scores for global equities by analyzing news articles, press releases, and regulatory disclosures using a proprietary transformer-based natural language processing model. Covering thousands of companies across major regions, it quantifies the tone and relevance of news events, offering granular sentiment metrics at both the entity and event level. By systematically capturing shifts in market sentiment and event novelty, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify potential price-moving signals, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk management. Its comprehensive coverage and advanced scoring methodology make it a valuable resource for predicting short-term and medium-term asset returns based on news-driven market dynamics.

name: Equity Alpha Factor Library
description: This dataset offers a comprehensive library of pre-calculated quantitative factors for equities, including financial ratios, valuation metrics, price and momentum statistics, analyst expectations, and industry-relative measures. Factors are constructed using point-in-time data and updated daily, covering profitability, growth, capital efficiency, valuation, earnings quality, volatility, analyst sentiment, and institutional ownership. By providing historical and current factor values, the dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to identify and backtest alpha-generating signals, construct multi-factor models, and enhance risk-adjusted return forecasts. Its breadth and granularity make it a powerful resource for systematic investment strategies and for predicting future price movements based on fundamental, technical, and behavioral drivers.

name: Performance-Weighted Analyst Estimates
description: This dataset applies an enhanced version of the StarMine SmartEstimate model to a broad universe of stocks and financial metrics, leveraging analyst estimate data from IBES. It calculates a performance score for each analyst based on their historical forecasting accuracy and incorporates the recency of their estimates. By combining these two factors, the model generates "smart estimates" that are more predictive than simple consensus means. The dataset includes modules for analyst innovation, outlier handling, and time-series feature generation, making it a robust tool for identifying which analyst forecasts are likely to be most accurate. This can help investors and researchers anticipate earnings surprises and price movements, as changes in smart estimates often precede market reactions.

The data is structured to support global asset allocation, cross-border valuation, sector and industry analysis, and derivatives research. By tracking changes in consensus, estimate revisions, and aggregated sentiment, the dataset enables investors to identify under- or overvalued markets, monitor macro and sector trends, and anticipate shifts in market sentiment—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements at both the index and sector level.

description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, the dataset is essential for ensuring data consistency and completeness in quantitative models and operational processes that rely on both Bloomberg and Reuters identifiers.

name: ESG Model
description: This dataset provides comprehensive Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factor scores for publicly traded companies worldwide. It includes detailed metrics across the E, S, and G pillars, such as board diversity, environmental efficiency, workforce equality, and shareholder rights, along with integrated ratings that combine financial and extra-financial health. The data is structured for quantitative analysis, enabling users to assess a company’s sustainability profile and long-term risk. By incorporating these ESG factors into investment models, analysts can identify companies with superior sustainability practices, which have been shown to correlate with improved risk-adjusted returns and can be used to predict future price movements and portfolio performance.

name: Analyst estimates & financial ratios
description: This dataset contains detailed point-in-time company financials, standardized ratios, earnings estimates, consensus recommendations, and business intelligence for global equities. It includes annual and interim financial statements, key ratios (such as ROE, ROA, debt-to-equity, margins), analyst estimates, and consensus ratings, as well as company reference data and officer information. The breadth and depth of financial metrics, combined with historical and restated data, allow for robust factor modeling, backtesting, and cross-sectional analysis. Researchers can use this dataset to identify value, growth, quality, and momentum signals, assess earnings surprises, and construct predictive models for price movements based on fundamental drivers and analyst sentiment.

name: Integrated Broker Estimates
description: WQ SmartData is an intermediate data platform that provides value-added, idea-embedded data managers and analytics for financial and event datasets. It includes advanced processing such as event classification (e.g., M&A, earnings), group clustering, natural language processing of textual data (e.g., EDGAR filings, news sentiment), and graph/network analytics. By integrating and transforming raw data from sources like FactSet, RavenPack, and EDGAR, it enables researchers to extract features, signals, and event-driven alphas that are difficult to obtain from raw feeds, supporting innovative quantitative strategies and improving the predictive power of models for price movements.

Reliable identifier mapping is a foundational tool for any workflow that involves multi-source data analysis or model building, indirectly supporting more accurate and robust price movement predictions by ensuring data integrity.

name: Dividend estimation data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg identifiers for financial securities. It is essential for cross-referencing and integrating data from different financial data providers, enabling analysts and systems to unify disparate datasets for more robust analysis. While it does not directly contain price or fundamental data, its utility lies in facilitating accurate data merging, which is crucial for building reliable models and conducting multi-source research that can ultimately improve price movement predictions.

name: Fundamental Analyst Estimates
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global companies, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. The dataset includes restatements, detailed line items, and standardized fields, enabling robust cross-company and cross-market comparisons. Key fields include balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as derived ratios such as return on equity, margins, and growth rates. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and predictive modeling, as it allows users to track historical financial performance, identify trends, and build factor models that can help forecast future price movements based on company fundamentals.

description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events that are likely to move markets. Each event is tagged by topic (such as M&A, earnings guidance, product launches, regulatory actions, and more) and assigned a significance level, allowing users to filter for the most impactful developments. The data includes detailed headlines, descriptions, event categorization, and metadata such as company identifiers, event timing, and industry classification. By focusing on material news and filtering out less relevant information, this dataset enables quantitative analysts and traders to integrate event-driven signals into their models, backtest the impact of specific news types, and react quickly to market-moving corporate actions, thereby improving the prediction of short-term price movements and volatility.

name: Daily Split Data
description: This dataset provides daily records of stock split and capitalization change events for global equities, including effective split dates, split factors, and related adjustment information. The data enables users to accurately adjust historical per-share financial measures (such as earnings per share, book value per share, and dividends per share) to reflect changes in share count due to splits. By ensuring that historical data is consistently adjusted for corporate actions, this dataset is essential for maintaining the integrity of time series analysis, backtesting, and quantitative models. Accurate split adjustment is critical for predicting price movements, as it prevents artificial jumps or drops in per-share metrics and allows for meaningful comparison of financial performance over time.

name: Smart Conference call transcript data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive coverage of corporate and macroeconomic events, including earnings releases, conference calls, IPOs, SEC filings, and economic indicators. It includes detailed event metadata, verbatim transcripts, analyst briefs, and supporting materials such as presentations and audio recordings. The data is structured with identifiers like RIC, CUSIP, SEDOL, and ISIN, and is updated frequently with both current and historical records. By tracking the timing, content, and sentiment of key corporate events and macroeconomic announcements, this dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate market-moving news, assess management tone and guidance, and identify catalysts that may impact stock prices and market volatility.

name: Europe Analyst Estimate Daily Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive statistics on the historical performance of equity analysts and their affiliated institutions (estimators) in the European market, focusing on price target forecasts and recommendations. It includes detailed metrics such as forecast accuracy (probability of price targets being met under different rules), revision accuracy, forecast consistency (measured by the stability of forecast errors), and profitability (average daily returns from following analyst forecasts or recommendations). The data is structured to allow ranking and normalization of analyst performance relative to peers covering the same stock, enabling identification of top-performing analysts and brokers. By quantifying the predictive skill and reliability of individual analysts and institutions, this dataset is highly valuable for constructing analyst-weighted forecast models, filtering signals by historical accuracy, and enhancing price movement prediction by leveraging the track record of those making the forecasts.

name: Fundamental Income and Dividend Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) for financial securities. Sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, it enables users to cross-reference and integrate data from these two major financial data providers. The mapping is essential for data normalization, security master management, and ensuring consistency across different data feeds and analytics platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, this dataset is a critical infrastructure component for quantitative research, portfolio management, and any workflow that requires accurate security identification and linkage across systems.

name: Standardized Analyst Consensus Forecasts
description: This dataset provides standardized, cleaned, and event-aligned analyst consensus forecasts and actuals for global equities, enabling direct comparison across companies and time. It aggregates and harmonizes consensus data from multiple leading sources, including I/B/E/S, Capital IQ, and FactSet, and applies rigorous data cleaning to remove expired or irrelevant forecasts. The dataset supports flexible configuration for different forecast horizons (quarterly, annual, rolling) and includes both forecast and actual values, as well as surprise calculations. By offering time-series event data with consistent methodology, it allows users to track revisions, analyze forecast accuracy, and construct robust quantitative models. This makes it a valuable resource for predicting price movements, backtesting strategies, and understanding market expectations versus realized outcomes.

name: Global Analyst Earnings Forecasts
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global analyst earnings forecasts, consensus estimates, and actuals for over 60,000 companies, sourced from broker and sell-side analyst submissions. It includes detailed and summary-level data on key financial metrics such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, and segment-level results, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The dataset tracks both current and historical estimates, revisions, and company-issued guidance, with extensive metadata on contributors, accounting standards, and industry classifications. By aggregating and updating analyst expectations in near real-time, this dataset enables users to monitor market sentiment, identify earnings momentum, and anticipate potential surprises—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing quantitative investment strategies.

name: Global Analyst Factor Signals
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of analyst-derived quantitative factors and indicators for global equities, constructed using standardized methodologies. It leverages consensus estimates, actuals, and revision data from multiple sources to generate a wide range of predictive signals, such as estimate momentum, earnings surprise, and analyst recommendation trends. The dataset is designed to be comparable across regions and time, with rigorous data cleaning and normalization. By offering both raw and composite factors—similar to those used in established quantitative models—this resource enables users to systematically test and implement alpha strategies, enhance risk models, and improve the forecasting of price movements based on analyst behavior and expectations.

name: Multi Horizon Analyst Revision Signals
description: This dataset provides decomposed analyst revision signals across short, medium, and long time horizons, derived from a comprehensive analyst revision-based stock ranking model. By applying advanced signal processing techniques, it extracts horizon-specific components from a wide array of analyst-driven metrics, such as earnings estimate changes, recommendation shifts, and predicted surprises. The resulting fields enable researchers and investors to isolate and analyze the impact of analyst sentiment and estimate revisions over different time frames, enhancing the ability to identify timely alpha opportunities and anticipate price movements driven by changes in analyst outlook. This multi-horizon approach is particularly valuable for constructing and testing trading strategies that are sensitive to the timing and persistence of analyst-driven signals.

name: Deep Learning Chart-Based Alpha
description: This dataset leverages deep learning to predict future stock returns by mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders who analyze price charts. It transforms time series financial data into images (such as OHLC or other chart types) and applies pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to these images to generate return forecasts. The output includes both raw return predictions and quantile-based relative return rankings, along with associated probabilities. By capturing complex visual patterns and technical signals that may be overlooked by traditional quantitative models, this approach can identify non-linear relationships and subtle chart features that are predictive of price movements. The dataset is particularly useful for developing and testing alpha models that seek to exploit behavioral and technical trading signals, offering a novel perspective that complements standard factor-based or fundamental models.

name: Price Chart Continuation Pattern Similarity
description: This dataset provides daily, per-stock similarity scores that measure how closely a stock’s price chart matches well-known continuation-style technical patterns, such as flags, pennants, rectangles, channels, scallops, staircases, cup-and-handle, and gap formations. The scores are derived by comparing chart-image embeddings to a curated library of canonical continuation patterns using advanced machine learning techniques. Multiple summary statistics (mean, median, max, dynamic, etc.) are available across different time horizons and regions, enabling flexible analysis. These similarity scores can be used to identify stocks likely to resume their current trend after consolidation, support trend-following strategies, and enhance alpha generation by confirming or filtering trading signals. The dataset is particularly valuable for quantitative researchers seeking to incorporate pattern-based insights into predictive models for price movement forecasting.

name: Digital Advertising Spend Intelligence
description: This dataset provides comprehensive estimates of digital advertising spend and related metadata across a wide range of websites and social media platforms, including details on brands, categories, channels, creatives, and purchase paths. It tracks ad impressions, spend, creative types, and the route each ad takes from advertiser to publisher, offering granular insights into advertising strategies and market presence. By analyzing trends in ad spend, creative deployment, and targeting strategies, researchers can gauge shifts in marketing intensity, brand competition, and consumer engagement, which may serve as leading indicators for price movements in related equities or sectors. The dataset is particularly valuable for identifying changes in digital marketing activity that could signal upcoming shifts in company performance or market sentiment.

name: Deep Learning Risk Free Returns
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict risk-free returns by transforming time series price and volume data into 2D chart images, which are then analyzed using pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The dataset includes predictions for multiple time horizons (such as 5, 10, 20, and 50 days) and provides both raw and relative return forecasts, along with quantile rankings and associated probabilities. By simulating a retail trader’s perspective through chart-based analysis, this dataset offers a unique, high-dimensional approach to forecasting future returns with minimal risk. It is particularly useful for identifying low-risk trading opportunities and enhancing portfolio construction by providing robust, model-driven signals that can help anticipate price movements in a risk-averse manner.

name: International Findings Data
description: This dataset offers daily snapshots of international corporate events, including earnings announcements, conference calls, dividend declarations, shareholder meetings, and other key financial events. It provides detailed metadata such as event status, timing, fiscal period, and confirmation level, along with links to press releases and filings. By tracking the timing and revisions of earnings dates, dividend actions, and other corporate events, the dataset enables researchers and traders to anticipate market-moving disclosures, identify signals of management intent, and exploit calendar-based trading strategies. Its forward-looking coverage and granular event data are valuable for predicting price movements, volatility spikes, and abnormal returns around scheduled corporate actions.

name: Global Earnings Call Sentiment Matrix
description: This dataset provides a structured, matrix-format aggregation of global company earnings call transcripts, focusing on sentiment and topic analytics. It leverages advanced natural language processing to extract and quantify positive, neutral, and negative sentiment probabilities from management presentations and Q&A sessions, across over 200 thematic topics. The data is filtered and enhanced with smart aggregation techniques, including rolling and daily sentiment measures, confidence scores, and relevance indicators. By capturing nuanced shifts in management tone and analyst reactions, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify patterns and signals that may precede price movements, offering valuable insights for predictive modeling and alpha generation in equity markets.

name: Multi Aspect Earnings Call Sentiment
description: This dataset provides advanced, multi-aspect sentiment analysis of earnings call transcripts for thousands of public companies across the US and Europe. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing and knowledge distillation from large language models, it evaluates sentiment across key financial dimensions such as asset utilization, profitability, leverage, valuation, and cash flow. The transcripts are segmented into presentation, question, and answer sections, with chunk-wise and summary sentiment scores available for each. Binary indicators and relevance scores help filter for the most impactful segments. By quantifying positive, negative, and neutral sentiment at granular and summary levels, the dataset enables investors and researchers to detect shifts in management tone, analyst sentiment, and market outlook, providing valuable signals for predicting future price movements and earnings surprises.

name: Machine Learning Company Event Signals
description: This dataset applies advanced machine learning and clustering techniques to structured company event text data, such as earnings calls, conferences, board meetings, and corporate actions. Unlike general news or social media, these events are high-quality, targeted, and often have direct implications for company performance and stock price movements. By extracting and modeling time-series features from these events, the dataset generates predictive signals that can be used to anticipate market reactions and inform trading strategies. The coverage includes a broad universe of companies and event types, making it a valuable resource for quantitative researchers seeking to enhance alpha generation through event-driven modeling.

name: Text-Based Event Relationship Analysis
description: This dataset leverages advanced language models to extract and classify relationships between companies, events, and entities from unstructured text sources such as news articles, press releases, and corporate communications. By identifying the types and directions of these relationships, the dataset provides structured insights into how companies interact, form alliances, or respond to market developments. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in company relationships—such as mergers, partnerships, or competitive actions—often precede significant market reactions. The dataset enhances traditional event-driven strategies by offering a deeper, more nuanced understanding of the connections and influences within the market ecosystem.

name: Corporate Event Sentiment Signals
description: This dataset provides structured sentiment analysis and key driver metrics derived from corporate event transcripts, including earnings calls, company presentations, analyst/investor days, and guidance calls. It covers a global universe of public companies, with detailed metadata such as industry classification, identifiers, event timestamps, and document sections. The dataset quantifies sentiment at multiple granularities—overall, by section, and by key topic—using scores based on positive and negative event counts, polarity, and word counts. By capturing management and analyst tone, margin and pricing power sentiment, and deception signals, it enables investors and researchers to assess market expectations, information asymmetry, and the impact of qualitative disclosures on price movements. These insights can be used to forecast earnings surprises, volatility, and post-event price drift, supporting both discretionary and quantitative investment strategies.

name: Global Institutional Fund Holdings
description: This dataset provides daily, account-level insights into the holdings and transactions of major institutional investors, including mutual funds, ETFs, asset managers, pension funds, and insurance companies. It features detailed tables on daily trades, holdings, and the size of the investment account panel, with metrics such as conviction holdings, boundary trades, significant transactions, and concentration measures. By tracking changes in institutional ownership, trade activity, and portfolio concentration, the dataset enables users to identify shifts in market sentiment, detect accumulation or liquidation trends, and assess the impact of large fund movements on individual securities. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, understanding liquidity dynamics, and generating alpha through analysis of institutional behavior.

name: Management and Executive Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive biographical and professional information on board members and senior executives from companies worldwide. It includes details such as employment history, education, achievements, compensation, board roles, committee memberships, and network connections across organizations. By analyzing board composition, director expertise, compensation structures, and interlocking directorates, investors and researchers can assess governance quality, leadership stability, and potential strategic shifts. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in executive leadership, board structure, or director networks often precede significant corporate actions, impact investor sentiment, and influence firm performance.

name: Direct Fundamental Data
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global equities, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for emerging markets. The dataset includes restated data from 2004 onward, ensuring historical accuracy and comparability. Key fields cover balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as detailed breakdowns of assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, and key performance indicators. FactSet’s symbology enables robust cross-referencing with other datasets. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and model development, as it allows researchers to track company financial health, valuation, and performance over time, supporting predictive modeling of price movements based on changes in core financial metrics.

name: Systematic mining of earnings calls data
description: This dataset provides sentiment scores and related metrics derived from the systematic analysis of corporate earnings calls. It leverages advanced natural language processing techniques to evaluate the tone, readability, and content of both the presentation and Q&A sections of earnings calls, including speaker-specific sentiment changes (e.g., CEO vs. others). The dataset covers a broad universe of companies across major global regions and includes both historical and daily updates. By quantifying management sentiment and communication style, this data can help investors anticipate market reactions to earnings disclosures, identify shifts in executive outlook, and enhance predictive models for stock price movements around earnings events.

name: Company Fundamental Data for Equity
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time global company fundamental data, capturing daily snapshots of financial statements, balance sheets, cash flows, and key ratios as they were known to the market at each historical date. It includes restatements, amendments, and all changes, ensuring accurate backtesting and minimizing look-ahead bias. The dataset covers a wide range of standardized and normalized financial metrics across regions and industries, making it a critical resource for quantitative research, factor modeling, and alpha generation. By reflecting the true information set available to investors at any given time, it enables robust prediction of price movements and supports the development of systematic investment strategies.

name: Accrual based Earnings Model
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of company fundamental data, including annual and interim financial statements, key ratios, per share data, and restatements. It includes detailed balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as derived metrics such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and valuation ratios. The data is available from 1980 for developed markets and from the 1990s for developing markets, with annual restatements starting in 2004. Each record is linked to unique entity and security identifiers, enabling robust mapping and time-series analysis. This dataset is essential for quantitative and fundamental research, allowing users to assess company financial health, detect trends, and build predictive models for price movements based on historical and point-in-time financial performance.

name: Governance, Accounting, Management, and Equality
description: This dataset provides quantitative model outputs for global equities, leveraging a model ensemble meta-algorithm that combines robust linear regression and a modified xgBoost classification approach. It includes a wide array of fundamental, accounting, governance, and management quality signals, as well as risk and event indicators such as bankruptcy, fraud, and executive turnover. The model is designed to predict three-month ahead stock returns and the likelihood of negative corporate events, offering daily cross-sectional scores and risk metrics. By integrating these diverse factors, the dataset enables users to identify stocks with superior governance, accounting quality, and management efficiency, as well as to anticipate adverse events, making it a powerful tool for forecasting price movements and constructing risk-aware equity portfolios.

name: Earnings Tax Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time fundamental financial data for public companies worldwide, with annual history dating back to 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. It includes detailed financial statement items, ratios, per-share data, and key performance indicators, all mapped to unique company and security identifiers. The data covers balance sheets, income statements, cash flows, segment information, and restatements, enabling robust analysis of company performance, valuation, and risk. By offering granular, timely, and historically consistent financial metrics, this dataset is essential for building and backtesting quantitative models, screening for investment opportunities, and forecasting price movements based on fundamental drivers.

name: Global Seasonal Regime Return Signals
description: This dataset provides predictive return signals for global equities by modeling the impact of calendar seasonality, corporate event timing, market regime context, and key data sources such as price-volume, analyst forecasts, options, and fundamentals. Each module isolates a specific data aspect—like price-volume trends, analyst revisions, or option-implied signals—and overlays contextual features such as month/quarter effects, proximity to earnings or guidance events, and prevailing market regimes (e.g., risk-on/off, expansion/contraction). The dataset is strictly point-in-time and D1-lagged to avoid lookahead bias, making it robust for research and production use. By enabling detailed analysis of how individual features and market contexts drive return predictions, it supports advanced quantitative modeling, event studies, and adaptive strategies across diverse market conditions.

name: Oil Price Resilience Scores
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), facilitating seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. By enabling accurate identification and linkage of securities, the dataset supports portfolio managers, analysts, and researchers in consolidating data from multiple sources, improving data quality, and reducing operational risk. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity in multi-source quantitative models and for efficient trade execution and compliance reporting.

name: Smart Insider Transaction Aggregates
description: This dataset provides a structured, matrix-format view of insider trading activity, where individual transactions by company insiders are aggregated and filtered using advanced methodologies. By summarizing key metrics such as average shares bought or sold, and applying smart filters to highlight the most relevant transactions, the dataset enables researchers and investors to efficiently identify patterns of insider behavior across companies and regions. Such aggregated insider activity is a valuable signal for predicting future price movements, as it can reveal informed trading ahead of significant corporate events or shifts in company fundamentals. The matrix structure makes it easier to incorporate these insights into quantitative models and backtesting frameworks, supporting the development of alpha-generating investment strategies.

name: Aggregated Insider Transaction Matrix
description: This dataset provides a structured matrix of insider transaction data, organized by company, region, and time delay. It aggregates and filters insider buying and selling activities, capturing key metrics such as average buy and sell values, transaction counts, and ratios over configurable time windows. By summarizing insider trades from individuals with privileged access to non-public information, the dataset enables analysts to identify patterns of opportunistic or routine trading, cluster buying, and other signals that may precede significant price movements. The smart aggregation and filtering enhance signal quality, making it a valuable resource for predicting future stock performance, detecting market anomalies, and constructing alpha-generating investment strategies.

name: Global Insider Transaction Aggregates
description: This dataset provides a structured matrix of aggregated insider transaction data across global markets, utilizing advanced filtering and smart aggregation techniques. It captures detailed information on insider trades, including buy and sell activity, transaction types, insider roles, and trade significance, organized by region and time delay. By consolidating and summarizing insider trading patterns, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify potential signals of future price movements, such as cluster buying or selling by key executives. The aggregation and enhancement of raw insider data into a matrix format make it easier to analyze trends, detect anomalies, and generate predictive signals for alpha generation, supporting both event-driven and quantitative investment strategies.

name: Global Insider Trading Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), serving as a cross-reference for security identifiers across two major financial data platforms. It is essential for researchers, portfolio managers, and quantitative analysts who need to integrate or reconcile data from both Refinitiv and Bloomberg sources. By enabling accurate and efficient linkage of securities across systems, this mapping facilitates robust multi-source data analysis, backtesting, and model development, ultimately supporting more reliable and timely investment decision-making and price prediction workflows.

name: Insider Trading for Europe
description: This dataset provides comprehensive records of insider trading activity across listed companies in over 30 European countries. It includes detailed information on transactions by company insiders such as executives, directors, and major shareholders, covering asset types, transaction dates, volumes, prices, and insider roles. The data is updated both historically and in near real-time, enabling analysis of buying and selling patterns, consensus signals, and conviction levels. By tracking the timing and nature of insider trades, investors and analysts can identify potential informational advantages, anticipate market-moving events, and enhance predictive models for stock price movements, especially when combined with other fundamental or event-driven signals.

name: Fund Short Selling Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive daily intelligence on hedge fund and asset manager short positions across 2,600 securities in 30 countries, covering over 600 managers since 2012. It includes granular details such as open positions, recent trades, crowding metrics, sentiment scores, trade lengths, portfolio weights, and performance attribution at the manager, security, sector, and country levels. The data enables analysis of short interest, fund crowding, and manager conviction, offering insights into market sentiment and potential risk from crowded trades. By tracking changes in short positions, trade activity, and manager behavior, the dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying short squeeze risks, and constructing quantitative trading signals.

name: Institutional Ownership Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive mapping between various global security identifiers, including FactSet Permanent Identifiers (FSYM_ID), CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL, ticker symbols, Bloomberg FIGI, and RIC codes. It covers security, regional, and listing levels, and includes metadata such as active status, security type, exchange codes, and entity relationships. The dataset enables seamless cross-referencing and integration of securities data from multiple sources, supporting accurate identification and aggregation of financial instruments across platforms. This mapping is essential for data normalization, portfolio reconciliation, and linking market data, which helps analysts and quantitative models track securities consistently and improves the reliability of price movement predictions by ensuring correct instrument identification and aggregation.

The dataset’s unified format and broad coverage make it a powerful tool for predicting short-term price changes and enhancing trading strategies.

name: Sensitivity to the Inflation Change
description: This dataset provides stock-level sensitivity estimates to expected inflation, using changes in breakeven rates and advanced machine learning techniques such as elastic net regression. It covers a wide range of global equities and includes sector, country, and performance metrics, allowing users to analyze how individual stocks and sectors respond to inflationary pressures. By quantifying inflation beta and related exposures, the dataset is valuable for portfolio managers and analysts seeking to forecast price movements, manage risk, and implement tactical asset allocation strategies in environments with changing inflation expectations.

name: Interest Rate Sensitivity Measures
description: This dataset provides a stock-level measure of interest rate sensitivity using a forward-looking discounted cash flow (DCF) approach. By simulating changes in discount rates and incorporating analyst forecasts, it quantifies how sensitive a company's valuation is to shifts in interest rates. The dataset includes key metrics such as implied cost of equity, elasticity to rate changes, and sector-neutralized scores, making it highly relevant for understanding how macroeconomic shifts—especially in interest rates—may impact equity prices. Investors and analysts can use this information to identify stocks that are more or less vulnerable to rising rates, construct hedged portfolios, and enhance alpha generation by anticipating market reactions to monetary policy changes.

name: Stock Selection DL model
description: This dataset provides the outputs of a next-generation deep learning model designed for global stock selection with a focus on statistical arbitrage and mean reversion alpha. It includes both raw and processed model scores, updated daily and with monthly historical data, covering a broad universe of equities across multiple regions. The model leverages advanced neural network architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, transformers, and conformers, and is engineered to be interpretable and relatively uncorrelated with common equity style factors. The dataset is particularly valuable for systematic and high-frequency trading strategies, as it offers timely, actionable signals that can be used to enhance portfolio construction, manage risk, and exploit short-term price inefficiencies. By providing robust, data-driven alpha signals, this dataset can help predict price movements and improve trading performance.

name: Return prediction from conference call
description: The Reuters Fundamentals Point In Time dataset provides comprehensive, globally standardized financial statement data for public companies, capturing both originally reported and restated values as they were known at each historical date. It covers over 47,000 active and 15,000 inactive companies across more than 100 countries, with daily updates and history extending back to 1989 for US firms and 1997 for non-US. The dataset is designed to eliminate forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate backtesting and robust quantitative research. By offering point-in-time snapshots of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, along with detailed metadata on restatements, reporting currency, and auditor opinions, it allows researchers and investors to model and predict price movements based on true historical financial information, supporting factor research, event studies, and systematic investment strategies.

name: Geographic network based model
description: This dataset contains daily momentum signals derived from networks of economically and fundamentally linked companies, spanning multiple regions and market segments. It combines seven distinct network-based momentum factors—such as business segment, geographic, analyst coverage, executive/board membership, innovation, supply chain, and shipping relationships—into a composite model using risk parity optimization. The resulting signals are designed to deliver stronger performance and lower downside risk than traditional price momentum, with demonstrated diversification benefits and high risk-adjusted returns. By capturing information spillovers and lead-lag effects across related firms, this dataset provides powerful predictive insights for systematic equity strategies, helping investors identify stocks with persistent return potential and manage portfolio risk more effectively.

name: Individual Investor Transactions Data
description: This dataset captures detailed transaction-level activity from over 81,000 individual retail users, including actions such as opening, closing, and adjusting positions, as well as watchlist modifications. It includes granular information on trade execution, portfolio types, user engagement metrics, and asset identifiers, updated frequently to reflect real-time investor behavior. By analyzing patterns in retail trading flows, sector allocations, and geographic distributions, this dataset offers valuable insights into sentiment shifts and crowd-driven market dynamics, which can be leveraged to anticipate short-term price movements and identify emerging trends in equity markets.

name: Search Engine Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC) for financial securities. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring broad coverage and accuracy. The mapping enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities across different data platforms, which is essential for data normalization, portfolio management, and multi-source analytics. While not directly predictive of price movements, this dataset is crucial for ensuring data consistency and reliability when combining datasets from various vendors, thereby supporting robust financial research and analysis workflows.

name: Earnings and conference call data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between two major financial security identifiers: RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) and Bloomberg ID. Covering a wide range of global securities, it enables users to cross-reference and integrate data from different financial data providers and platforms. By facilitating seamless linkage of market data, pricing, and reference information across systems, this mapping is essential for data normalization, portfolio management, and multi-source analytics. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is a foundational resource for building robust, integrated datasets that support advanced financial modeling, risk analysis, and trading strategies.

name: Chart Pattern Similarity Scores
description: This dataset provides daily similarity scores that quantify how closely a stock’s recent price chart matches a range of canonical bilateral technical patterns, such as triangles, wedges, V-formations, and gap structures. By leveraging advanced image-based embeddings of OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) data, the dataset compares current price action to a curated library of reference patterns, producing scores for each pattern and aggregation method (mean, max, quantile, etc.) across multiple time horizons and global regions. These similarity scores help researchers and traders identify when a stock is exhibiting chart formations that historically precede significant price moves, either as continuations or reversals. The dataset is particularly valuable for developing and validating quantitative trading signals (alphas), as it enables systematic pattern recognition, supports cross-sectional and multi-horizon analysis, and can be integrated into machine learning models to enhance predictive power for future price movements.

name: Predictive Analyst-Company Signal Set
description: This dataset provides predictive signals specifically designed for advanced analyst and company relationship modeling, leveraging deep learning on company relations and analyst estimate data. It enhances traditional analyst revision and valuation models by integrating both company-to-company (Revere) and analyst-to-company (IBES) information, resulting in higher quality and broader coverage signals, especially for global equities. The dataset includes modules that generate forward-looking signals based on changes in analyst sentiment, earnings revisions, and valuation metrics, all informed by the underlying network of business relationships. These predictive signals can be used to anticipate future price movements by capturing both direct analyst actions and the economic linkages between companies, offering a unique edge for quantitative price prediction and alpha generation.

name: Price Volume Data for Equity
description: The dataset contains financial data related to equities, including metrics such as prices (open, high, low, close), trading volumes, market capitalization, returns, dividends, splits, and other key indicators that provide insights into stock performance and market activity.

name: Interval and MOO&MOC statistics
description: This dataset provides comprehensive intraday market data at interval levels, including order imbalance events, quote and trade ticks, and detailed auction data for Market-On-Open (MOO) and Market-On-Close (MOC) sessions. It covers multiple global exchanges and includes fields such as bid/ask prices and sizes, trade prices and volumes, auction prices and volumes, and various qualifiers for trade and quote conditions. The dataset also tracks session-level statistics, volatility, VWAP, and order book dynamics. By analyzing order imbalances, auction outcomes, and interval-based price and volume movements, users can identify periods of heightened buying or selling pressure, anticipate price swings around auction events, and detect liquidity shifts. This information is highly valuable for predicting short-term price movements, understanding market microstructure, and developing intraday trading strategies.

name: Microstructure Spread Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive spread pricing data for securities traded across the US, Canada, and Asia. It includes key fields such as the ticker symbol, the spread (difference between bid and ask prices), and spread values calculated over the last 30 minutes, both in absolute terms and in basis points. By analyzing the spread and its recent changes, traders and analysts can gauge market liquidity, trading costs, and potential price volatility. Narrowing or widening spreads can signal shifts in supply-demand dynamics, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying periods of heightened market activity.

name: Bond Yield Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive reference and pricing information for global corporate bonds, including historical data since 2006. It covers a wide range of attributes such as unique identifiers (ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL), issuer details, bond characteristics (coupon, maturity, callable/putable status), industry classifications, and extensive pricing fields (open, high, low, last, bid, ask, mid, volume, yields). The inclusion of corporate actions, structured note features, and regulatory indicators (such as IRS 871(m) compliance) makes it a robust resource for fixed income analysis. By leveraging this dataset, analysts can track bond performance, assess credit risk, monitor liquidity, and identify market trends, all of which are critical for predicting price movements and making informed investment decisions in the corporate bond market.

name: Relationship Data for Equity
description: This dataset provides a mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC), enabling users to link securities across Bloomberg and Refinitiv platforms. The data is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, and maintained for integration and operational purposes rather than general research. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for harmonizing datasets, ensuring accurate cross-platform security identification, and supporting multi-source data analysis in quantitative research and portfolio management workflows.

name: Equity Warrants Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs for securities, facilitating cross-platform identification and integration. It is particularly useful for analysts and systems that require harmonization of security identifiers across different data sources, enabling seamless data aggregation, reconciliation, and analysis. While it does not contain direct market or price data, its utility lies in supporting accurate linkage of datasets, which is essential for robust multi-source financial research and for ensuring consistency in price movement prediction models that rely on data from both Refinitiv and Bloomberg ecosystems.

name: Intermediate Cluster Groups
description: This dataset compiles relationship scores between companies using textual analysis of regulatory filings such as Form 10-K, Form 20-F, Def-14A, and streetevents transcripts. It includes both manually curated and algorithmically extracted relationships, providing a rich view of inter-company connections. The dataset is particularly useful for identifying strategic partnerships, competitive threats, and supply chain links, which can influence price movements and inform event-driven trading strategies.

name: Corporate Bond Pricing Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of equity signals derived from corporate bond pricing data, including z-spread curves, term spreads, and principal component analysis factors such as shift, tilt, and twist. By linking bond market indicators—such as credit risk, yield curve dynamics, and bond-equity return divergences—to related equities, the dataset offers 19 base factors and several variants to predict future stock returns. These factors capture changes in credit conditions, market sentiment, and cross-asset relationships, making the dataset valuable for quantitative models, risk assessment, and alpha generation. Investors and analysts can use these signals to enhance equity selection, construct long-short strategies, and anticipate price movements based on underlying credit market trends.

name: Daily Spot and Cross Rate Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized global company fundamental data, covering 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and interim/quarterly financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and textual information for over 1500 data items. The data is point-in-time, capturing values as they were known historically, and supports peer comparability across regions and industries. With detailed income statements, balance sheets, cash flows, and supplemental metrics, this dataset enables robust analysis of company financial health, valuation, profitability, and risk. It is highly valuable for quantitative research, backtesting, and building predictive models to forecast price movements based on changes in fundamentals, financial ratios, and corporate actions.

name: Derived Industry Classification
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, two of the most widely used security identifiers in the financial industry. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of data from different sources, facilitating more accurate and efficient data analysis. This mapping is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who work with multi-vendor data feeds, as it ensures consistency in security identification across platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is essential for data normalization, aggregation, and the construction of robust multi-source trading and risk models.

name: Alternate Industry Classification
description: This dataset provides an alternative industry classification for global equities, derived from historical stock returns using principal component analysis (PCA) and robust resampling methods. By extracting significant risk factors and grouping securities into clusters of varying sizes, it offers a data-driven approach to industry segmentation across multiple regions and sectors. The dataset includes detailed mappings for top securities and supports flexible cluster sizes, enabling users to analyze market structure, sector rotation, and cross-sectional risk. This classification can enhance factor modeling, portfolio construction, and alpha generation by capturing dynamic relationships between stocks, potentially improving predictions of price movements and risk exposures.

name: Specific Return Dataset
description: This dataset provides daily specific returns for global equities, calculated using a proprietary risk model that extends the Barra framework with additional style and industry factors. The data includes returns orthogonal to risk model factors, representing the idiosyncratic or residual component of asset performance. Coverage spans multiple regions and universes, with fields such as Bloomberg ID and specific return percentage. By decomposing total returns into factor-driven and residual parts, this dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to isolate stock-specific movements, assess alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted forecasting of price changes.

name: Europe Relation Dataset
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive, real-time text news feed combining Dow Jones and Reuters NewsScope content. It includes news headlines, full stories, alerts, and updates from major financial newswires, with extensive tagging for companies, topics, regions, and events. The feed covers a wide range of asset classes, sectors, and geographies, and is structured for both human and machine consumption. With rich metadata, including RICs, topic codes, and timestamps, the dataset enables event detection, sentiment analysis, and thematic research. Its breadth and timeliness make it valuable for predicting price movements, as news events, corporate actions, and macroeconomic developments often drive short-term and long-term market reactions. The dataset is suitable for quantitative models, trading strategies, and risk management that rely on news flow and event-driven signals.

name: Multi-Domain Quantitative Factor Library
description: This dataset is a comprehensive library of quantitative factors designed for stock selection and risk modeling across global equities. It integrates hundreds of signals derived from regulatory filings, institutional ownership, sector-specific metrics, technical indicators, sentiment analysis, patent data, and alternative sources. The factors span multiple domains, including banking, technology, real estate, health care, and energy, and leverage both numerical and textual data using advanced techniques such as natural language processing and network analysis. By providing diverse, uncorrelated signals and sector-specific insights, the dataset enables investors and researchers to enhance alpha generation, improve risk management, and develop robust predictive models for price movements in various market environments.

name: Securities Lending Insight Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) for global securities. It enables seamless integration and reconciliation of security data across different financial platforms and data sources. By facilitating accurate cross-referencing, the dataset supports portfolio management, trade processing, and data aggregation tasks. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity and consistency when combining datasets for quantitative research, risk analysis, and multi-source analytics.

name: Daily Specific Return Profiling Dataset
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized fundamental financial data for companies worldwide, covering over 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and interim/quarterly financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and extensive historical content. The data is point-in-time, capturing values as they were known at each reporting date, and includes restatements and amendments. With over 1,500 data items, it enables in-depth analysis of company performance, valuation, profitability, liquidity, leverage, and growth. The breadth and depth of coverage, along with proven peer comparability, make it a critical resource for building and backtesting quantitative models, identifying fundamental drivers of price movement, and constructing factor-based investment strategies.

name: Specific return of extended factors
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of analyst earnings estimates, company-issued guidance, and actual reported financials for over 60,000 companies. It includes both detailed and consensus forecasts for key financial metrics such as EPS, revenue, cash flow, and dividends, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The data is updated daily and includes historical records, point-in-time snapshots, and restated values to avoid look-ahead and survivorship bias. Industry classification is available via TRBC, and the dataset supports granular analysis by region, sector, and fiscal period. By tracking estimate revisions, consensus trends, and the relationship between guidance and market expectations, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements around earnings announcements, identifying sentiment shifts, and constructing alpha models based on analyst behavior and forecast dispersion.

name: Other Multi-Factor Risk Models
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of analyst estimates, actuals, recommendations, and price targets for over 60,000 companies. It includes both detailed (analyst-by-analyst) and consensus (mean, median, standard deviation) forecasts for key financial measures such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, dividends, and long-term growth. The data is updated daily and includes historical records, company-issued guidance, and surprise calculations (actual vs. consensus). With granular detail on estimate revisions, analyst and broker identities, and industry classifications, this dataset is essential for tracking market expectations, identifying earnings momentum, and quantifying earnings surprises—factors that are highly predictive of short-term and medium-term price movements. The breadth and timeliness of the data make it a cornerstone for quantitative models, event studies, and backtesting strategies that rely on forward-looking market sentiment and analyst behavior.

name: Rapid Search Interest Signals
description: This dataset captures real-time search interest data for specific companies and regions, using a standardized algorithm to transform hourly search trends into a continuous, unbounded metric. By estimating daily search activity from high-frequency data and providing a confidence score for each estimate, it enables timely detection of shifts in public attention or sentiment. Such rapid changes in search volume can serve as early indicators of market-moving events, news, or shifts in investor sentiment, making the dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and generating alpha signals.

name: Website Popularity Rankings
description: This dataset provides a robust, research-oriented ranking of the most popular websites worldwide, designed to be resistant to manipulation and volatility. It aggregates and harmonizes data from multiple sources, including DNS traffic, browser extensions, and web crawls, to produce a stable and reproducible list of top domains. The dataset includes detailed metrics such as relative popularity, ranking intervals, domain counts, and statistical measures like skewness and kurtosis. By mapping domains to standardized identifiers, it enables aggregation and analysis at various levels. This dataset is valuable for predicting price movements by identifying trends in web traffic, shifts in user behavior, and the emergence of influential domains, which can signal changes in market sentiment, consumer interest, or sector performance.

name: Sentiment Data by NLP
description: This dataset offers a reliable mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv. It enables seamless cross-referencing of securities across major financial data platforms, supporting integration and reconciliation in research, trading, and portfolio management systems. While not intended for general research or alpha generation, the mapping is essential for ensuring data consistency, linking disparate datasets, and facilitating accurate security identification in multi-vendor environments.

description: This dataset tracks daily Wikipedia page views for a global universe of companies, including both parent entities and their subsidiaries. Spikes or changes in page views can signal increased market interest, news events, or shifts in company visibility, which may precede trading activity or price movements. The dataset is especially useful for generating alternative sentiment signals and for event-driven trading strategies, as it captures real-time shifts in public focus that are not reflected in traditional financial data.

name: Securities Lending Files Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of securities lending activity across equities and fixed income instruments in over 110 countries. It aggregates transaction-level data from lending agents, third-party lenders, and beneficial owners, as well as borrowing activity from prime brokers and asset managers. Key fields include loan volumes, loan rates (average, min, max, and dispersion), utilization rates, collateral types, and borrowing activity ratings. The dataset also tracks the supply of shares available for lending, loan recalls, and rate changes, offering both daily and intraday granularity. By analyzing metrics such as utilization ratios, loan rate spikes, and borrowing demand, investors can identify securities under short-selling pressure, detect scarcity premiums, and anticipate potential price movements due to short squeezes or changes in market sentiment. This makes the dataset highly valuable for predicting price dynamics, managing risk, and developing alpha-generating strategies.

name: Sentiment Data for Equity
description: This dataset aggregates and analyzes social media posts and news articles related to financial markets, covering thousands of sources and several years of historical data. It quantifies market sentiment and buzz for individual assets, sectors, and indices using advanced natural language processing and machine learning techniques. The data includes sentiment scores, buzz indicators, and trading signals, which are statistically validated and can be used to identify shifts in market mood, anticipate volatility, and generate actionable buy/sell signals. By monitoring real-time and historical sentiment, traders and analysts can enhance their price movement predictions and improve portfolio performance through timely, data-driven decisions.

name: Investor views
description: This dataset tracks the co-search behavior of users on a major financial platform, capturing which companies are most frequently searched together by retail investors. By analyzing the top co-searched tickers for each focal stock, the data reveals patterns of investor attention, perceived relationships between companies, and potential information diffusion across stocks. Such insights can be valuable for predicting price movements, as spikes in co-search activity may signal increased investor interest, sector rotation, or anticipation of news events, all of which can lead to short-term price pressure or comovement among related stocks.

name: Deep Learning Stock Clusters
description: This dataset groups stocks into clusters using deep learning models that analyze 2D images generated from time series financial charts. By mimicking the perspective of retail traders, the dataset leverages convolutional neural networks to extract learned representations from price and fundamental chart images, then applies advanced clustering techniques such as k-means++ and dimension reduction. The resulting clusters reflect similarities in stock behavior, sector, and other financial characteristics, providing a high-dimensional, feature-rich grouping beyond traditional sector classifications. These clusters can be used to identify homogenous groups of stocks, improve portfolio diversification, and enhance risk modeling. By understanding how stocks are grouped based on complex chart patterns and features, analysts and quants can better predict price movements, uncover new sources of alpha, and construct more robust trading strategies.

name: US Stock Search Trend Matrix
description: This dataset transforms web search trend data for the top 3000 US stocks into structured fields suitable for financial analysis. By leveraging daily and hourly search popularity scores for company names and ticker symbols, it provides a time series of public interest in individual stocks, including coverage on weekends and holidays. The data is normalized and decomposed to facilitate robust comparisons and feature generation, making it easier for researchers to extract meaningful signals. Increased search activity can reflect shifts in investor attention or sentiment, which may precede price movements, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term and long-term stock returns.

name: Deep Learning Technical Indicator Returns
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze images of technical indicator charts, mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders. By converting time series financial data into 2D images, pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used to predict future stock returns and their relative rankings across multiple time horizons. The dataset provides quantile-based return predictions, confidence scores, and cross-sectional rankings for a diversified universe of global equities. Its image-based approach captures complex market patterns and technical signals that may be missed by traditional time series analysis. This can be highly valuable for forecasting price movements, generating alpha signals, and constructing systematic trading strategies with improved prediction accuracy and low correlation to conventional models.

name: Global Workforce Flow and Skills Analytics
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, monthly-tracked information on workforce dynamics, including headcount, inflows, outflows, seniority, roles, skills, salaries, and prestige across thousands of companies and regions. It aggregates data from online professional profiles and job postings, standardizing job titles and skill clusters for robust cross-company and cross-industry analysis. The dataset includes detailed metrics on employee transitions, skill acquisition, layoffs, and sentiment from employee reviews, offering granular insights into talent flow, workforce optimization, and organizational health. By monitoring changes in hiring, attrition, and skill trends, investors and analysts can identify early signals of operational strength or weakness, anticipate company performance shifts, and enhance fundamental models for predicting stock price movements.
